extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and peer reviewers for Research Project Grants (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH definitions and reviewer guidance for assessing Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), including overall impact and review criteria, plus mechanism-specific considerations and additional review topics (human subjects, animals, biohazards, resource sharing, budget, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: Assess likelihood to exert sustained, powerful influence on the field, considering criteria below. R15: Assess likelihood to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the institution's research environment, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 supports discrete, well-defined projects that can be completed in two years with limited funding; applications may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification may be provided through literature citations, external data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R15 objectives: provide support for meritorious research, strengthen the research environment of schools not major NIH recipients, and expose undergraduate/graduate students to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available. Reviewers should consider effect on strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new models, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications need not have extensive background or preliminary information; reviewers will focus on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to significantly advance knowledge. Appropriate justification via literature or available data is acceptable. Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning Grant) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials including team establishment, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategies, protocol finalization, and operations manual preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not designed for collection of preliminary data or pilot studies to support trial rationale. Reviewers focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 variant: Also consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will substantially strengthen the school/academic component and expose students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? For Early Stage Investigators or those early in independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? For established investigators, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects assess complementary and integrated expertise, leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure. R15 variant: Also assess whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether concepts/approaches/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, and whether a refinement, improvement, or new application of these is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early-stage development, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage risky aspects? If human subjects/NIH-defined clinical research, evaluate plans to address 1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and 2) inclusion/exclusion based on sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children, justified in terms of scientific goals and strategy. R15 clinical research wording: evaluate protection of human subjects and inclusion of minorities and both sexes/genders and children. R15 also: does the application provide sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate student interest toward biomedical/behavioral science careers?

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources adequate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project will benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements. R15 variant: evaluate likely availability of well-qualified students to participate and whether students have in the past or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, the committee will evaluate justification for involvement of human subjects and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For research meeting exemption categories, evaluate: 1) justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials. See 'Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposed projects involve human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as inclusion (or exclusion) of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation determines if inclusion/exclusion is justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy. See 'Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five points: 1) proposed use of animals, species/strains/ages/sex/numbers; 2) justification for use and appropriateness of species and numbers; 3) adequacy of veterinary care; 4) procedures for limiting discomfort/distress/pain/injury (including use of analgesic/anesthetic/tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices); and 5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. See 'Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards are identified, reviewers will determine whether adequate protection is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior critiques and whether changes address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prior accomplishments and how they support the proposed continued work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the revision relates to a specific line of investigation in the original application that was not recommended for approval, the committee will consider whether responses to previous review comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether such opportunities are not readily available in the United States or whether they augment existing U.S. resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided regarding Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes: 1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, 2) registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, 3) procedures to monitor possession, use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and 4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans - Data Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Data Sharing Plan, or the rationale for not sharing data, is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment concerns the reasonableness of plans to share data or the justification for not sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans - Sharing Model Organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the plans for sharing model organisms, or the rationale for not sharing them, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on whether mechanisms for sharing model organisms are appropriate or whether a rationale for not sharing is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans - GWAS/Genomic Data Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS) / Genomic Data Sharing Plan, or the rationale for not sharing, is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the adequacy and reasonableness of genomic data sharing plans or justifications for not sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether requested funds and duration align appropriately with proposed activities and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comments can include suggestions for improvement, concerns, or explicit recommendations about resubmission.
